question.text: Under the SOP for default by a TM or CM, SEBI requires exchanges to settle the credit balances of which category of investors as an interim measure?

answer.text: Small investors with balances less than Rs. 25 lakh are settled first using unencumbered deposits; investors with balances exceeding Rs. 25 lakh are paid on a pro-rata basis
All investors are settled equally regardless of balance size
Only institutional investors are settled first since they have larger exposures
No interim settlement is made; all claims go through the normal arbitration process

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the Series VIII workbook (page 182), in case of a TM/CM default the exchange first settles the credit balances of small investors with balances less than Rs. 25 lakh using unencumbered deposits available with the exchange. Investors with balances exceeding Rs. 25 lakh are paid on a pro-rata basis from the remaining funds. The Trap: Small investors (balances < Rs. 25 lakh) are settled first; larger investors are paid pro-rata from what remains. Equal or institution-first treatment, or waiting only for arbitration, does not match the SOP. Note: The Rs. 25 lakh threshold and the unencumbered-deposits-first sequence are the key elements of the interim settlement rule.
